newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open easier on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open easier on consolidation.

text.p: French shares showed modest losses at the opening on Friday, with operators taking profits and allowing the market to consolidate.
Traders said franc softness and settlement today were factors steering the market lower, along with a cautious Wall Street.
The franc has eased in the last few days on jitters caused by calls for a depreciation in the franc to help spur growth.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 9.75 points or 0.44 percent at 2,223.82 at 0910 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,228 from 2,238.5 on Thursday's close.

Water company Lyonnaise des Eaux was among few gainers, up 0.39 percent, helped by news it is buying out minority shareholders in its Elyo heating subsidiary, to simplify the group structure and focus on main businesses.
Eurotunnel fell 1.32 percent, continuing the week's weakness since a fire disrupted service.
Alcatel Alsthom bucked the trend, strengthening 1.72 percent. One market source said the stock has benefited from U.S. buying.

Another source said Alcatel may also be helped by a new fraud inquiry by a Paris judge involving Jean-Luc Lagardere, chairman of Lagardere Groupe, which could raise hopes of a re-opening of the Thomson SA sale.
